candidates.abstract: Sparse tensor compilers are commonly used high-performance tools that optimize tensor algebra programs over notoriously complex sparse data structures. Despite the ever-increasing size and scale of sparse datasets, there exists astonishingly little research on developing a parallel sparse tensor compiler. Existing approaches fail to parallelize or make assumptions about access patterns or output formats that limit generality. This paper presents Birdseed, the first tensor compiler to support all loop orderings over any standard sparse format in parallel. More specifically, Birdseed supports parallel sparse scatters and directly writes into list, bytemap, hash, and dense levels of fibertree sparse formats. Our approach exhibits asymptotic memory and time improvements over all previous work. We additionally demonstrate empirical speedups on challenging kernels to parallelize, such as histogram construction and SpMSpV.

contribution.en: Introduces Birdseed, the first tensor compiler supporting all loop orderings and parallel sparse outputs over standard sparse formats.
contribution.zh: 提出 Birdseed，首个支持所有循环顺序和任意标准稀疏格式并行稀疏输出的张量编译器。

why_care.en: Directly relates to tensor compilers, sparse code generation, and parallel compilation.
why_care.zh: 直接关联张量编译器、稀疏代码生成与并行编译。

candidates.title: Parallel Sparse Outputs for Tensor Compilers

candidates.abstract: Many important computational workloads are bound by the performance of the memory system that supplies data to conventional processors. Compute in Memory (CiM) promises to circumvent this bottleneck by performing the processing within the memory. Neural Networks are memory-bound, and a notable example of such is the Hopfield Network. This work explores the design space of non-volatile computing-in-memory (NV-CiM) architectures using an instruction-level simulator to evaluate application mappings and workload-driven architectural adaptations. The exploration examines the resulting design trade-offs and includes theoretical comparisons with representative CPU and GPU architectures.

contribution.en: Explores NV compute-in-memory architecture design space for Hopfield networks via an instruction-level simulator.
contribution.zh: 用指令级模拟器探索基于非易失存储器的 Hopfield 网络计算内存架构设计空间。

why_care.en: Adjacent to PIM/CIM and memory-centric architectures, though not compiler-centric.
why_care.zh: 邻近研究兴趣中的 PIM/CIM 与内存中心架构，但不涉及编译器核心。

candidates.title: Hopfield Networks in Non-volatile Memory

candidates.abstract: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs requires jointly optimizing tensor, pipeline, expert, context, and data parallelism alongside micro-batch size, recomputation, sharding, and overlap, a combinatorial space where memory legality can hinge on a single byte of activation accounting. Today, teams navigate it through expensive multi-node trial and error, burning GPU-hours on crashes and suboptimal recipes. We present Primus Projection, which closes this loop with two coupled components. First, a hybrid projection engine that measures what it can and simulates what it cannot: GPU microbenchmarks on as few as a single device capture compute kernels and any in-scope communication; a sub-node downscale-measure-upscale workflow analytically restores out-of-scope collectives, FSDP overlap, and the full pipeline schedule at the multi-node target. A pure simulation mode runs entirely on CPU, enabling pre-silicon planning without any GPU. Second, the Primus Tuning Agent treats the projection engine as a fast scoring oracle (seconds per candidate instead of tens of minutes) and uses it to drive an intelligent search over the configuration space. A deterministic seed planner sweeps single axes; an LLM investigation loop proposes cross-axis combinations the planner cannot reach, with an analytic memory pre-filter that rejects infeasible candidates before any GPU time is spent. Validated on Llama 3.1 (dense) and Mixtral 8x22B (MoE) across two GPU generations, all projections stay within ~10% of measured multi-node throughput, and fidelity holds at production scale: 4.7% error on DeepSeek V3 671B at 1,024 GPUs and 1.9% on Qwen3-235B-A22B at 256 GPUs. In a Mixtral 8x22B case study, the Primus Tuning Agent discovers a configuration delivering +27% throughput over the published 4-node BF16 reference at the same scale, in under 30 minutes of single-node exploration.

contribution.en: Presents Primus Projection, coupling a projection engine with an auto-tuning agent to search distributed LLM training configurations.
contribution.zh: 提出 Primus Projection，结合投影引擎和自动调优代理来搜索分布式 LLM 训练配置。

why_care.en: Related to parallelism/autotuning, but focused on distributed training systems rather than compilers.
why_care.zh: 与并行/自动调优相关，但主要面向分布式训练系统而非编译器。

candidates.title: Beyond the Trial-and-Error Loop: Hybrid Projection and Automated Tuning for Distributed Training

candidates.abstract: LLM agents are evolving from a single model calling tools to planners that orchestrate multiple expert models whose capabilities live in distinct weights. This shift breaks a hidden assumption of today's serving systems: that the working set of models fits in GPU memory. On the memory-constrained GPUs typical of private and edge deployments, naive whole-model swapping serializes weight transfer with computation and, without host-backed KV restoration, discards session state at a switch. We present JointServe, a serving system that treats weight shards and KV blocks as residency objects competing for one unified memory budget. JointServe exploits three structural properties of agent workloads (directed calls, gapped execution, and dual-state residency) to prepare models before they are called: an intent signal parsed from the caller's own output stream triggers prefetch during generation, partial k* residency reduces switching to incremental layers, and a preemptive transfer scheduler protects live-session KV with a guaranteed bandwidth share. A carve-out control step adjusts the weight/KV allocation as workload demands change. Evaluations show that JointServe reduces session completion time by 21.7% over the strongest whole-model swap baseline and stays usable in a crash regime where every whole-model swap baseline fails to finish (a 46-fold gap). On replayed SWE-bench, tau-bench, and OSWorld traces, it cuts session completion time by up to 49% and lifts SLO attainment from 2.8-24.5% to 76.8-100%.

contribution.en: Proposes JointServe, managing weight shards and KV blocks as residency objects for multi-model agents on memory-constrained GPUs.
contribution.zh: 提出 JointServe，在显存受限 GPU 上按驻留对象管理权重分片与 KV 块以服务多模型智能体。

why_care.en: Belongs to serving systems and GPU memory management, distant from compiler research.
why_care.zh: 属于服务系统与 GPU 内存管理，与编译器研究距离较远。

candidates.title: JointServe: Serving Multi-Model Agents on Memory-Constrained GPUs

candidates.abstract: Lane-based RISC-V vector processors exploit data parallelism well but pay a recurring cost for two common patterns: reductions, which require a separate tree pass, and deep dependent expression chains, which cannot be fused and are issued as serial vector instructions. We present TALU, a 5-stage RISC-V core whose execute stage is an NxN grid of registered ALU tiles instead of a single ALU. The grid is a reconfigurable, feed-forward spatial fabric: tiles route operands only from non-backward neighbours, and added diagonal forwarding lets a reduction collapse spatially. A minimal custom extension configures the per-tile operation, routing, and per-tile constants, and streams operands through the array. On a single fabric, TALU runs ordinary scalar code, single deep-path expressions, and multi-lane vector kernels. On the benchmark suite of the RISC-V2 vector processor, TALU is 1.8-5.5x faster than RISC-V2 and 4.5-15.5x faster than Vicuna at equal lane count, with a reduction cost (dot{\div}add) of 1.05x versus 1.96x and 1.26x for the vector cores. A retimed implementation places and routes at 1.03 GHz in 45 nm in 0.30 mm2, half the area of RISC-V2.

contribution.en: Introduces TALU, a reconfigurable N×N ALU-grid execute stage for RISC-V that accelerates reductions and deep dependent expressions.
contribution.zh: 提出 TALU，一种面向 RISC-V 的可重构 N×N ALU 网格执行级，加速规约和深依赖表达式。

why_care.en: Relevant to computer architecture, SIMD, and compiler-architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 与计算机体系结构、SIMD 和编译器-架构协同设计相关。

candidates.title: TALU: A Reconfigurable Tiled-ALU Grid for RISC-V

candidates.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) serving systems must balance latency and throughput while efficiently utilizing distributed GPU resources. This challenge arises because inference consists of two fundamentally different phases: prefill, which determines time-to-first-token (TTFT), and decode, which determines inter-token latency (ITL). The use of tensor parallelism (TP), pipeline parallelism (PP), and hybrid configurations exposes different trade-offs between these latency dimensions, making the optimal parallelism configuration highly dependent on workload characteristics, latency requirements, and context length. Moreover, despite the widespread adoption of distributed inference, there is still limited understanding of how parallelism configurations should be selected under varying workload conditions and service-level objectives (SLO). In this paper, we develop a systematic framework for characterizing LLM inference parallelism via throughput-latency trade-offs, SLO-aware serving, and long-context scalability. We introduce the notion of parallelism operating regions by constructing TTFT-ITL feasible sets and Pareto frontiers across different workload compositions, thereby revealing a systematic transition from TP-dominant to PP-dominant configurations as workloads become increasingly prefill-heavy. We further formulate SLO-aware parallelism selection using goodput, showing that stringent TTFT requirements favor PP-dominated configurations, whereas relaxed latency constraints progressively shift the optimality toward TP-dominated configurations with higher serving capacity. Finally, we demonstrate that increasing context length fundamentally changes the relative advantages of parallelism configurations, with PP-dominant configurations exhibiting more favorable scalability and SLO attainment in the long-context regime.

contribution.en: Systematically characterizes throughput-latency trade-offs and SLO-aware selection for tensor and pipeline parallelism in LLM inference.
contribution.zh: 系统刻画 LLM 推理中张量并行与流水线并行的吞吐-延迟权衡及 SLO 选择。

why_care.en: Involves parallel computing and GPU serving performance, but not compilers or IR optimization.
why_care.zh: 涉及并行计算与 GPU 服务性能，但非编译器或 IR 优化。

candidates.title: Scaling LLM Inference via Parallelism: Throughput-Latency Trade-off

candidates.abstract: Thermal constraints in heterogeneous multi-core systems can significantly degrade performance, as conventional techniques such as dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and task migration introduce overhead under high utilization. Approximate computing, particularly loop perforation, can mitigate this overhead by reducing computation at the cost of accuracy loss. However, existing approaches typically apply a uniform perforation rate across all loops, ignoring loop-specific sensitivity. We propose AMAX, an accuracy-aware multi-loop asymmetric perforation framework that reduces the combinational design space through loop-wise profiling and multi-objective configuration selection, and dynamically adapts the resulting configurations at runtime according to performance requirements. Experiments on PARSEC benchmarks show that {\em AMAX} achieves up to 0.85 improvement in normalized accuracy over symmetric perforation for the same performance targets.

contribution.en: Introduces AMAX, performing accuracy-aware asymmetric loop perforation via loop-wise profiling and multi-objective configuration selection.
contribution.zh: 提出 AMAX，基于循环级剖析与多目标配置选择实现精度感知的非对称循环穿孔。

why_care.en: Adjacent to loop transformation, approximate computing, and heterogeneous architecture optimization.
why_care.zh: 邻近循环变换、近似计算与异构体系结构优化。

candidates.title: AMAX: Accuracy-Aware Multi-Loop Asymmetric Perforation for Heterogeneous Architectures

candidates.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are moving onto edge devices, but little is known about how much energy they draw on single-board computers with NPU or GPU accelerators, or where that energy goes. We measure total-system energy, latency, and thermal behavior of Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and its text-only sibling on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-10H NPU and on a Jetson Orin Nano Super, on both CPU and accelerator, and separate the fixed energy of each request from the energy that grows with output length. Because the accelerators use different quantization and serving software, we compare deployment stacks rather than silicon. Three findings stand out. First, NPU offloading makes the Pi a much more efficient VLM platform: it cuts energy per generated token by about two-thirds, leaves the host CPU largely free, and avoids the thermal throttling that the CPU backend reaches in sustained use. Second, an image adds both fixed and per-token energy, but at typical response lengths generating the answer costs far more than processing the image. Third, the Jetson GPU favors short responses through its lower fixed cost per request, whereas the Pi NPU favors longer ones through its lower cost per output token; their energy curves cross near 40 output tokens.

contribution.en: Measures total-system energy, latency, and thermal behavior of VLM inference on Raspberry Pi NPU and Jetson GPU platforms.
contribution.zh: 在树莓派 NPU 与 Jetson GPU 上测量 VLM 推理的系统能耗、延迟和热行为。

why_care.en: Edge energy characterization, weakly related to core compiler/architecture interests.
why_care.zh: 属于边缘能效测量，与编译器/体系结构核心兴趣关联很弱。

candidates.title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms

candidates.abstract: NVIDIA Grace--Blackwell systems make CPU--GPU memory increasingly unified at the programming level, but unified addressability does not make the memory system uniform. A CUDA managed allocation on GB200 may be served from GPU-local HBM, accessed through host/system memory, demand-migrated, prefetched, reused after GPU access, or evicted and reloaded under capacity pressure. The problem is that these states share a programming interface while exercising different hardware paths and runtime mechanisms, making a single ``Unified Memory bandwidth'' number misleading. This paper presents a placement-controlled microbenchmark study of CUDA Unified Memory on NVIDIA GB200, using GH200 as a Grace--Hopper baseline and GB10/DGX Spark as a validation platform. Our methodology separates local HBM access, host/system-memory access, explicit movement, managed first touch, prefetch, reuse, access-pattern sensitivity, oversubscription, and CPU--GPU handoff, then summarizes the observations with a measurement-calibrated model of compute, access, migration, eviction, synchronization, and handoff costs. On GB200, a 1~GB STREAM-style triad reaches 3963~GB/s from local HBM but 304~GB/s through host-mapped CPU/system memory; for a 256~MB streaming kernel, cold CPU-initialized managed memory reaches 14.1~GB/s, while managed prefetch and reuse reach 4606~GB/s and 4504~GB/s. Below the capacity boundary, prefetched and reused managed memory remain above 4.6~TB/s, but at 125\% of CUDA-visible memory they fall to 968~GB/s and 1214~GB/s, showing that Grace--Blackwell unified memory must be understood through placement, access history, locality, reuse, and capacity pressure.

contribution.en: Characterizes GB200 Unified Memory performance across local HBM, host-mapped, migration, prefetch, reuse, and oversubscription states via placement-controlled microbenchmarks.
contribution.zh: 通过受控微基准刻画 GB200 统一内存在本地 HBM、主机映射、迁移、预取和超容量压力下的性能状态。

why_care.en: Provides a measurable model of placement and access-history costs relevant to GPU memory management and compiler/runtime decisions.
why_care.zh: 为 GPU 内存放置与运行时/编译决策提供可迁移的测量模型。

candidates.title: Understanding NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell Unified Memory Through Placement-Controlled Microbenchmarks

candidates.abstract: AI workloads increasingly employ low-precision formats such as BF16 / FP16, FP8 variants, FP4, Micro Scaling (MX), and INT modes across models, layers, and execution stages to balance accuracy, memory footprint, and throughput, which in turn requires hardware to support these formats in a flexible and efficient way. We present MFSA, a weight-stationary multi-format systolic array that achieves area efficiency through two architectural choices. At the PE level, MFSA uses dot-product-accumulator-based processing elements extended from an existing open-source trans-precision FPU to support reduced-precision formats (FP32/FP16/BF16/CFP8/FP4/INT16/INT8/INT4) with a shared datapath and proportional throughput scaling. At the array level, MFSA employs Online Block-Scale Rebasing (OBSR) for block-scaled formats, which folds each block scale into the running FP32 partial sum at block boundaries without adding a second cross-block accumulator, thereby reducing the additional overhead of block-scaling support. In TSMC 28 nm at 1 GHz, matched-throughput BF16/FP8/FP4 cascaded FMA-PE baselines are 1.5x/2.5x/4.5x larger than the single-format DPA-PE, the gap growing with subword parallelism. A routed 16x16 MFSA reaches a peak 0.5/1/2/4 TOPS of FP32/BF16/FP8/FP4, and OBSR cuts the incremental MX overhead by 64.2% in area and 67.5% in energy versus a naive MX implementation baseline, without hurting the numerical stability on real LLM traces. Adding support for all other formats based on a BF16+CFP8 systolic array costs 25.7% additional area. OBSR also extends to non-power-of-two block scales: folding the fractional part of an E4M3 scale into the MFPE dot product supports NVFP4 alongside OCP MX for 11.8% area and 7.3% power over a CFP8+FP4 base, less than half the cost of a naive implementation.

contribution.en: Presents a weight-stationary multi-format systolic array with online block-scale rebasing to support BF16/FP8/FP4/MX/INT modes efficiently.
contribution.zh: 提出支持 BF16/FP8/FP4/MX/INT 等多格式的权重固定脉动阵列，并用在线块缩放重定基降低 MX 开销。

why_care.en: Its multi-format datapath and block-scale folding inform low-precision accelerator compilation and hardware abstraction.
why_care.zh: 其多格式数据通路与块缩放折叠对低精度加速器编译和硬件抽象有参考价值。

candidates.title: MFSA: A Multi-Format Systolic Array with Native Micro Scaling Support

candidates.abstract: The rapid adoption of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and long-context LLMs has shifted the computational burden toward the prefill phase---the initial stage where the model processes all input tokens in parallel before generating a response---yet its energy impact remains poorly characterised. We investigate the contradiction between massive hardware-level power spikes and the sub-linear marginal cost of input tokens reported in system-level studies. Through high-resolution telemetry of Llama-3.1 and Qwen-2 models on NVIDIA A100 hardware, we identify the efficiency threshold where $O(n^2)$ attention complexity overcomes GPU parallelisation. Our results quantify how optimised memory orchestration (PagedAttention) delays this scaling bottleneck across three orders of context scaling, yielding up to an 8.9$\times$ energy efficiency advantage at 112,000 tokens compared to standard baselines. Furthermore, we characterise the energy disparity between input and output tokens, demonstrating that optimised serving (vLLM) causes this ratio to narrow (from $\approx$850$\times$ to 750$\times$) as context scales due to high decode efficiency, whereas unoptimised baselines show a much smaller, roughly constant gap ($\approx$150--230$\times$) because their prefill is itself expensive. This work establishes context-scaling laws that differentiate engine-level optimisations from inherent model constraints, providing an empirical framework for sustainable LLM deployment.

contribution.en: Profiles energy of input-token prefill in LLMs and derives context-scaling laws separating engine optimizations from model constraints.
contribution.zh: 通过遥测分析 LLM 预填充阶段输入 token 的能耗，并区分引擎优化与模型固有约束的上下文扩展规律。

why_care.en: Offers empirical energy data for LLM serving memory orchestration, but is far from the compiler/IR core.
why_care.zh: 为 LLM 服务的内存编排与能效评估提供经验数据，但与编译器/IR 主线距离较远。

candidates.title: The Cost of Context: Profiling the Energy Footprint of Input Tokens in Large Language Models

candidates.abstract: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.

contribution.en: Introduces a retraining-free differentiable elasticization method that turns a pretrained Transformer into one model adaptable across compute budgets.
contribution.zh: 提出免重训练的可微弹性化方法，将预训练 Transformer 剪成可在多种计算预算下即时调整的单一模型。

why_care.en: Belongs to model compression/elastic inference, only indirectly inspiring for compiler optimization.
why_care.zh: 属于模型压缩/弹性推理方向，对编译器优化只有间接启发。

candidates.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic

candidates.abstract: Equivariant interatomic potentials enable accurate and efficient simulations of molecules and materials. Among them, models based on SO(2) convolutions reduce the cost of tensor products and achieve state-of-the-art accuracy, but their training remains time-consuming and memory-intensive. Existing training implementations materialize large edge tensors for representation transformations surrounding dense matrix multiplications, increasing memory usage and data movement. We observe that these transformations can be integrated into the model's existing dataflow, avoiding separate intermediate materialization. We introduce TrimSO(2), a fast and memory-efficient algorithm for SO(2)-based equivariant models. It realizes this principle through rotation on gather, recombination with activation, and inverse rotation on reduction, with support for the higher-order differentiation required for training. By avoiding intermediate materialization, TrimSO(2) delivers 2.71-16.73$\times$ operator speedups across forward, backward, and double backward and reduces model-level high-bandwidth memory traffic by 3.81-9.88$\times$. Finally, TrimSO(2) achieves 2.07-2.94$\times$ training speedups and 1.53-3.16$\times$ reductions in peak training memory over PyTorch implementations for official eSEN, UMA, and EquiformerV3 workloads on A100 and H100 GPUs.

contribution.en: Integrates rotation, recombination, and inverse rotation into the existing dataflow of SO(2) equivariant models, avoiding edge-tensor materialization to speed training and cut memory.
contribution.zh: 将 SO(2) 等变模型的旋转/重组/逆旋转融入既有数据流，避免边张量物化，提升训练速度并降低显存。

why_care.en: Its materialization-avoiding dataflow transformation is transferable to tensor-program fusion and memory optimization.
why_care.zh: 其避免中间物化的数据流变换可迁移到张量程序融合与显存优化。

candidates.title: TrimSO(2): Fast and Memory-Efficient Training of Equivariant Interatomic Potentials

candidates.abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer great potential for low-power intelligent computing owing to their event-driven nature, yet their deployment is limited by high inference latency and inefficient hardware utilization caused by temporal dependencies. Existing accelerators struggle to balance timesteps, accuracy, and energy efficiency, while hardware-oriented timestep compression remains underexplored. To address these challenges, this work presents STISA, a unified algorithm-hardware co-design framework featuring: (i) a Temporal Splitter Compression (TSC) technique with a Temporal Split Structure (TSS) to reduce temporal redundancy while preserving network dynamics; (ii) a hardware-efficient spatiotemporal parallelism scheme, which co-optimizes dataflow and architecture through a Temporal-Prioritized Output-Stationary (TPOS) mapping and a flexible Block-Mux Streaming (BMS) architecture; and (iii) a joint TSC-TPOS-BMS co-optimization framework featuring a bandwidth-aware resource allocation strategy to achieve balanced accuracy, latency, and energy efficiency across diverse network architectures. On the algorithmic side, TSC reduces synaptic operations by 24.44%-51.71% while achieving competitive accuracies of 96.38%, 81.10%, 68.51%, and 82.40% on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet, and DVS-CIFAR10, respectively. On the hardware side, FPGA prototypes deliver up to 7.99 speedup, 30.4% power reduction, and 30.1% LUT reduction. Compared with state-of-the-art SNN accelerators, STISA achieves 0.16 GOPS/W/PE, demonstrating its scalability and superior energy efficiency for real-time SNN inference under constrained hardware resources.

contribution.en: Presents an algorithm-hardware co-design framework for SNNs with temporal split compression, spatiotemporal mapping, and bandwidth-aware resource allocation.
contribution.zh: 提出面向 SNN 的算法-硬件协同设计框架，含时间分裂压缩、时空并行映射与带宽感知资源分配。

why_care.en: Targets low-power SNN accelerator design, with weak ties to the compiler/IR core.
why_care.zh: 属于低功耗 SNN 加速器设计，与编译器/IR 主线关联较弱。

candidates.title: STISA: A 0.16 GOPS/W/PE Single-Shot Inference FPGA-based SNN Accelerator with Algorithm and Hardware Co-Design

candidates.abstract: Analog in-memory computing performs the matrix-vector multiplications of neural networks directly inside the memory array, which saves time and energy. But each memory cell stores only a few levels and is noisy, so one cell cannot hold a weight precisely. The standard fix is to split each weight across several cells, like digits of a number. The base of this split decides the trade-off: a large base gives fine resolution but amplifies the noise, and a base near one averages the noise but wastes resolution. The best-known prior analysis considers only the noise, and so it always picks a base of one. We propose a principled method that also accounts for the limited number of levels per cell. It gives the optimal base in closed form, from a single measurement of the device noise. On a device-physics simulator, the optimal split is 3.3 dB more accurate than the common base-16 split, and it beats equal splitting in end-application accuracy.

contribution.en: Derives a closed-form optimal weight-splitting base for matrix-vector multiply on noisy analog in-memory accelerators, trading cell levels against device noise.
contribution.zh: 为噪声模拟存内计算中的矩阵向量乘提出闭式最优权重拆分基，同时权衡单元电平数和器件噪声。

why_care.en: Relevant to in-/near-memory compilation and mapping, offering a clean closed-form device-level optimization.
why_care.zh: 与存内计算/近存计算的编译与映射问题相关，且以简洁闭式解给出器件级优化。

candidates.title: Closed-Form Optimal Weight Splitting for Matrix-Vector Multiply on Noisy In-Memory Accelerators

candidates.abstract: We introduce Continuum Attention (CA), a causal Transformer attention operator that replaces discrete key and value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve. Each query induces an exponential relevance density along the curve. Integrating the density and interpolated values yields exact normalized attention from closed form exponential moments, including half token boundary contributions. The gradients follow analytically from moments of order at most two, enabling parallel GPU implementations while retaining quadratic sequence complexity and the standard Transformer decoder. Compared with ordinary softmax and focal attention, CA reduces mean validation negative log likelihood by 0.0200 and 0.0480 nats per byte, respectively, winning all paired comparisons. An additional disjoint validation slice yields a 0.0457 nats per byte advantage over the strongest selected softmax baseline, with a paired 95% confidence interval. These findings motivate continuous integration as a promising attention alternative while leaving larger scale generalization open.

contribution.en: Introduces Continuum Attention, replacing discrete key/value lookup with integration over a continuous piecewise-linear memory curve using exponential moments.
contribution.zh: 提出连续注意力算子，用连续分段线性记忆曲线上的指数矩积分替代离散 key/value 查找。

why_care.en: Is a Transformer attention mechanism innovation, only indirectly related to compiler and architecture research.
why_care.zh: 属于 Transformer 注意力机制创新，对编译器与体系结构研究仅间接相关。

candidates.title: Continuum Attention

candidates.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. CAFE introduces C$^2$AM, a bit-significance-weighted conducting-cell activity metric that predicts output deviation and inference accuracy degradation under FeFET device variation. Guided by C$^2$AM, CAFE applies differential weight and activation encoding to eliminate sign-extension-induced conducting-cell amplification. To balance robustness and cost, CAFE performs type-wise encoding enumeration, layer-wise NSGA-II search, and post-GA pruning to allocate robust encodings where the robustness-cost trade-off is favorable. Across representative vision and language workloads, CAFE reduces C$^2$AM by up to $28.6\times$; in the main deployment study, it improves accuracy over two's-complement CIM by more than 87 percentage points and approaches full-differential robustness at $1.86$-$2.78\times$ normalized cost, compared with $3.06\times$ for uniform full-differential encoding.

contribution.en: Proposes conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding with C2AM for robust DNN inference in FeFET-based CIM.
contribution.zh: 提出面向FeFET CIM的导通单元感知自适应差分编码，用C2AM指导编码搜索以提升DNN推理鲁棒性。

why_care.en: Relevant to PIM/CIM architectures and compiler-architecture co-design, suggesting encoding and robustness optimizations for in-memory computing.
why_care.zh: 与PIM/CIM架构及编译器-架构协同设计相关，可启发面向存储内计算的编码与鲁棒性优化。

candidates.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory

candidates.abstract: An agent that drives an LLM sends the model the same conversation again and again, and each turn adds only a little text at the end. Inference engines reuse the KV cache of the shared prefix, so only the new tokens pass through the model. However, tokenization has no such shortcut. The CPU front end of the serving engine converts every request back into token IDs from its first character, which lengthens the time to first token (TTFT) and consumes CPU on every turn. We present Delta Tokenizer, a CPU tokenization front end that tokenizes only the delta between a request and the previous request of the same session. It retains the earlier token sequence, encodes again only the appended text and the short tail whose tokens the append could affect, and joins the two only at a position the tokenizer's splitting rules themselves cannot move, which keeps the result exact. For long requests with no state to reuse, it cuts the text where practical tokenizers already keep neighboring pieces independent, encodes the pieces on several cores at once, and concatenates the outputs into the reference encoding, exactly. A shared CPU pool schedules these chunks together with the short incremental updates, so an update runs between two chunks rather than behind an entire long job. The incremental path shortens the tokenization of a session turn by roughly 40x relative to the Hugging Face reference tokenizer, and on 16 cores the chunk-parallel path encodes a four-million-character request 8.2x faster than a serial encode and 1.6-2.1x faster than LoPT. Inside SGLang, Delta Tokenizer reduces the median TTFT through the chat interface by 59% at 100K tokens and brings the P99 TTFT of agent sessions down 9.5x under load and 23x when long requests tie up the front end. Every output we checked matches the reference, among them 41.8 billion documents encoded by its fast encoder.

contribution.en: Introduces incremental and chunk-parallel CPU tokenization front end that exactly reuses session prefixes and accelerates long-prompt preprocessing.
contribution.zh: 提出增量与分块并行的CPU分词前端，精确复用会话前缀并加速长提示预处理。

why_care.en: Parallel CPU preprocessing and long-sequence serving optimizations may transfer to parallel compiler/runtime pipelining.
why_care.zh: 并行CPU预处理与长序列服务优化可迁移到编译器/运行时并行流水线思路。

candidates.title: Delta Tokenizer: Reference-Identical Tokenization of Session Deltas and Segment-Parallelism for Long Prompts on Multicore CPUs

candidates.abstract: Sparse matrices, in which most entries are zero, are central to scientific simulation, graph analytics and machine learning, and their multiplication with dense inputs is a core parallel kernel. In many applications the matrix stays fixed while only a few input rows change per step, so the result can be updated from those rows alone, which we call the dirty set. Sparse kernels often add a second optimization based on the inspector-executor principle, in which a tiled schedule is prepared once and reused across calls. However, when this reuse remains profitable as the dirty set moves is not well characterized. In this paper, we show that retained tiled execution rarely beats direct CSC in incremental sparse matrix multiplication, although incremental execution itself remains highly profitable. Across 21 SuiteSparse matrices and controlled patterns of motion, a direct column-wise incremental update is 2.1-8.2x faster than the best of eight full-recomputation codes, among them Intel oneMKL and PyTorch. Yet the same direct update outperforms a tiled executor that retains tile preparation and caches assembled schedules in 779 of 837 workloads. Separating reuse into per-tile preparation and cached schedules shows that the benefit comes from preparation; extra cache capacity seldom helps because a tile set rarely returns after a different one has intervened. Tiling is faster only when tiles merge many entries into each output write, a structural property that we predicted before measurement and confirmed on four held-out matrices of the same family. These results show that the structure of the matrix and the motion of the dirty set, rather than the sophistication of the schedule, determine whether reuse is profitable. We anticipate that our methodology and guidelines will help developers decide when to build schedule reuse into incremental sparse runtimes.

contribution.en: Characterizes when schedule reuse pays off in incremental sparse matrix multiplication, finding direct column-wise incremental update often beats retained tiled schedules.
contribution.zh: 系统刻画增量稀疏矩阵乘中脏集移动与调度复用的收益边界，发现直接列式增量更新常优于保留分块调度。

why_care.en: Challenges assumptions about tiled schedule reuse in inspector-executor and parallel loop scheduling, informing compiler/runtime scheduling decisions.
why_care.zh: 对并行循环调度、检查器-执行器及分块复用假设提出反例，可指导编译器/runtime调度决策。

candidates.title: How the Dirty Set Moves: Characterizing Schedule Reuse in Incremental Sparse Matrix Multiplication

candidates.abstract: Closing the loop of AI-driven science requires reliably translating natural-language protocols into executable laboratory workflows despite protocol defects and heterogeneous hardware. Existing approaches often couple scientific interpretation with device-specific code generation, making errors difficult to localize and limiting reuse across laboratory platforms. We introduce LabCompiler, a robust protocol-to-execution framework that transforms imperfect natural-language protocols into verifiable human-machine workflows. Its protocol firewall diagnoses and repairs defects before compilation while preserving unaffected content, guided by troubleshooting knowledge accumulated through perturbation-guided self-evolution. A two-level, device-agnostic graph representation separates experimental semantics from hardware-specific implementation and supports capability-based device assignment with coordinated human execution. We further introduce a protocol recovery benchmark covering four controlled perturbation types and naturally occurring errors collected from protocols written by iGEM participants. Experiments show that LabCompiler outperforms frontier LLMs in protocol error correction while enabling coordinated human-machine execution across heterogeneous, partially automated laboratory settings.

contribution.en: Presents a compiler-style framework translating imperfect natural-language lab protocols into verifiable human-machine execution workflows.
contribution.zh: 提出将不完美自然语言实验协议转化为可验证人机实验流程的编译器式框架。

why_care.en: Its device-agnostic graph representation and repair pipeline offer distant analogies to heterogeneous compilation and IR design.
why_care.zh: 其设备无关图表示与错误修复流程与异构编译和中间表示设计有遥远类比。

candidates.title: LabCompiler: A Framework for Verifiable Human-Machine Laboratory Execution from Imperfect Protocols

candidates.abstract: Chance-constrained stochastic programs (CCSPs) require solutions that satisfy uncertain constraints with high probability. Standard approaches either embed scenarios directly into optimization by considering sample average approximation (SAA)-based reformulations, growing prohibitively expensive and often failing to find feasible solutions; or employ conservative reformulations that guarantee feasibility but sacrifice objective quality by design. We propose ACCESS (Adaptive Chance-Constrained Exploration via Structured Sampling), a structured sampling framework that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation. First, high-quality candidate solutions are generated by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, avoiding sampling directly in the constrained high-dimensional solution space. Second, feasibility is assessed separately via large-scale batched simulation over a massive number of scenarios, which is naturally amenable to GPU parallelism. That reduces the search from a high-dimensional solution space to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity; while concentrating on candidates near the feasibility boundary, where high-quality feasible solutions lie. We also introduce a variant, ACCESS($\delta$), which provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability $1-\delta$. Experiments across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions show that ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while ACCESS($\delta$) is empirically feasible on every instance. The conservative reformulations remain several percent worse in objective, and SAA is frequently infeasible while taking an order of magnitude longer on the harder benchmarks.

contribution.en: Proposes structured sampling framework decoupling chance-constrained optimization from feasibility evaluation via large-scale GPU simulation.
contribution.zh: 提出将机会约束优化与可行性评估解耦的结构化采样框架，并利用GPU大批量模拟评估可行性。

why_care.en: Methodological analogy to search-verification decoupling and GPU-parallel evaluation in compiler optimization.
why_care.zh: 与编译器优化问题中的搜索-验证解耦及GPU并行评估有方法论类比。

candidates.title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs

candidates.abstract: Data movement between memory and processing units remains a major bottleneck in data-centric systems. Memristive Stateful Logic (SL) addresses this problem by performing Boolean operations directly on stored resistive states. However, arithmetic efficiency depends jointly on the device-supported logic primitive set, the dependency structure of the resulting operation sequence, and its mapping to datapath architectures. While prior designs typically optimize device, logic, and architecture layers separately, we jointly consider them to co-design a stateful adder. We experimentally demonstrate a mixed MAGIC and FELIX logic primitive set on printed Electrochemical Metallization (ECM) memristors and derive a full adder sequence optimized for inter-bit carry propagation. Mapping this sequence to bit-serial, bit-parallel, and bit-pipelined datapaths reduces the latter two to 2n+6 cycles for an n-bit addition. For 32-bit addition, this requires 60-88% fewer cycles than prior SL adders. Across four representative workloads, we achieve 3.7x-16.4x speedup over prior. These results show how cross-layer co-design can translate into improved workload-level performance.

contribution.en: Co-designs printed memristor stateful logic adders across device, logic, and datapath layers, optimizing carry propagation for multiple datapath styles.
contribution.zh: 跨器件-逻辑-架构协同设计印刷忆阻器有状态逻辑加法器，优化进位传播并映射到不同数据通路。

why_care.en: Directly relevant to PIM/in-memory computing and accelerator cross-layer co-design, inspiring arithmetic and datapath mapping for emerging devices.
why_care.zh: 直接关联PIM/存内计算与加速器跨层协同设计，可启发面向新型器件的算术与数据通路编译映射。

candidates.title: Cross-Layer Co-Design of Low-Latency Stateful Logic Adders with Printed Memristors

candidates.abstract: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.

contribution.en: Introduces LayerTrim, a training-free structured pruning method that trims decoder MLP features while preserving long-form reasoning.
contribution.zh: 提出免训练结构化剪枝方法LayerTrim，选择性裁剪解码器MLP特征以保持长推理能力。

why_care.en: Weakly related to compilers/architecture; mainly background on model compression and inference efficiency.
why_care.zh: 与编译器/体系结构关联弱，仅可作为模型压缩与推理效率的背景。

candidates.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming

candidates.abstract: When writing code, the same computation can be expressed in different programming languages and through different implementation strategies. We show that the activations of LLMs capture this shared structure in reusable and composable abstract representations when they generate code. These representations emerge in the middle layers, are reusable across programming languages, and afford the model an impressive amount of generalization ability when generating code under various interventions. Using activation steering, we show that function, programming language, and implementation strategy can be independently manipulated. The independent interventions on language and function can be flexibly composed to control code generation, even in cases when the prompt contains no information about language and function. We additionally find that finetuning on examples of arbitrarily defined functions in one programming language transfers to other languages, consistent with the models reusing abstract features of code generation that are shared across different examples. Finally, to study how such abstract representations come to be, we implement a minimal model of shared, reusable, and composable structure in a synthetic setting, and show that transformers trained on such data learn representations that reuse these parts flexibly across contexts.

contribution.en: Shows LLMs form reusable, composable abstract representations during code generation, with function, language, and implementation strategy independently steerable.
contribution.zh: 揭示LLM在代码生成中形成可复用、可组合的抽象表示，并可通过激活干预独立操纵函数、语言与实现策略。

why_care.en: Potentially inspires abstraction and cross-language transfer in program synthesis and LLM-assisted code generation.
why_care.zh: 对程序合成与LLM辅助代码生成中的抽象表示和跨语言迁移有潜在启发。

candidates.title: LLMs program using Reusable and Composable Abstract Representations

candidates.abstract: The semiconductor workforce shortage has renewed interest in making chip design accessible to students without conventional very-large-scale integration (VLSI) training. We present the AI Hardware Design League (AI-HDL), an international, project-based competition in which students use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively refine Verilog while simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, security review, and physical verification provide the engineering feedback needed to validate the result. Across two annual cycles, AI-HDL grew from 172 to 604 participants and from 40 to 108 teams, reaching 30 universities, six community colleges, and 19 countries. In the 2026 cohort, 68.7% of participants reported no prior Verilog experience. Twenty-two teams completed the four design phases and reached final evaluation. Two division-winning designs completed physical sign-off in the SkyWater 130 nm (Sky130) process, passing design-rule checking and layout-versus-schematic verification with zero violations before being submitted for fabrication. These results show that an LLM-assisted, tool-grounded workflow can be deployed at substantial scale while also revealing that completion, rather than initial access, remains the principal challenge. AI-HDL materials and finalist artifacts are released to support replication and future study.

contribution.en: A large-scale competition shows LLM-assisted, tool-grounded Verilog generation can reach physical sign-off.
contribution.zh: 大规模竞赛表明，LLM辅助且工具闭环的Verilog生成可达到物理签核。

why_care.en: It touches LLM-based hardware design but not compiler optimization, IR, or code generation.
why_care.zh: 它涉及LLM辅助硬件设计，但不涉及编译器优化、IR或代码生成。

candidates.title: From Prompts to Silicon: Scaling LLM-Assisted Chip Design with the AI Hardware Design League

candidates.abstract: This paper presents CacheSmith, a KV cache reuse system for RAG prefill that maximizes quality-gated SLO attainment. While context caching lowers prefill latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks, it misses cross-chunk attention that a full prefill would compute over concatenated inputs. Prior selective recomputation schemes tackle this problem but enforce static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to effectively handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a three-phase workflow of WarmUp, Probe, and Patch that can be dynamically configured to exploit a wide range of cost-accuracy trade-offs. At serving time, an SLO-aware scheduler in CacheSmith forms batches to mitigate inter-request interference during layer-by-layer prefill, while a budget-aware planner configures recomputation phases across the batch to maximize the number of requests satisfying both generation quality and latency targets. Both components make fast, solver-free decisions over profiled cost-accuracy bands. On four benchmarks across varying arrival rates and burstiness levels, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%, over four state-of-the-art baselines.

contribution.en: A KV-cache reuse system dynamically trades recomputation against latency SLOs for RAG prefill.
contribution.zh: KV缓存复用系统在RAG预填充中动态权衡重计算与延迟SLO。

why_care.en: It is an ML serving optimization far from compiler IR, synthesis, or architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 这是ML服务优化，远离编译器IR、综合或架构协同设计。

candidates.title: CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse

candidates.abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

contribution.en: PolyNets embed known polynomial dynamics in a training-free tensor graph for neural emulation.
contribution.zh: PolyNets将已知多项式动力学嵌入免训练张量图以实现神经仿真。

why_care.en: It offers a GPU-friendly numerical-simulation formulation but is not compiler or architecture work.
why_care.zh: 它提供GPU友好的数值仿真形式，但不是编译器或体系结构工作。

candidates.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation

candidates.abstract: We introduce MorphingNet, a network for symbolic regression (SR) whose units change their function continuously. Instead of searching over expressions built from a fixed operator library, MorphingNet trains the form of each function as a parameter, so SR becomes one continuous optimization problem. Its units are either pole-free rational functions or complex exponential--logarithm functions, which move between exponentials, sinusoids, damped oscillations, power laws and logarithms as their parameters change. The network is a readable formula at every step of training, and no operator library is needed to train it; a structure-recovery step afterwards rewrites the trained formula into short elementary expressions. Training is dense linear algebra, so it is GPU-friendly and scales to large data. MorphingNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SRBench, recovers most generating formulas on synthetic benchmarks, and on large data is up to two orders of magnitude faster than the strongest search method. By turning the search for a formula into the training of a network, MorphingNet offers a new paradigm for SR and for scientific discovery from data.

contribution.en: MorphingNet turns symbolic regression into continuous network training with interpretable units.
contribution.zh: MorphingNet将符号回归转化为带有可解释单元的连续网络训练。

why_care.en: Its continuous optimization view could inspire synthesis/search methods, though it targets formulas not code.
why_care.zh: 其连续优化视角可能启发综合/搜索方法，但目标为公式而非代码。

candidates.title: MorphingNet: Symbolic Regression Where the Network Is the Formula

candidates.abstract: Transformer based intrusion detection has shown strong potential for identifying unknown malware variants, but its deployment on resource constrained edge devices remains difficult due to the high computational and memory cost of self attention. This paper presents an event sparse Linear Transformer framework for malware detection on FPGA edge platforms. Instead of relying on an explicit attention matrix, the proposed method derives token and channel importance directly from the accumulated key value state of Linear Transformer. A contribution aware scoring function is introduced to measure the perturbation of each token or kernel channel to the linear attention state, allowing redundant tokens and low contribution channels to be removed without constructing quadratic attention maps. To translate sparsity into practical hardware acceleration, the proposed design further replaces conventional binary mask based execution with a Top K active token buffer and a hardware compaction unit. The selected active tokens and channels are reorganized into dense fixed length data streams, enabling downstream processing elements to execute regular multiply accumulate operations with reduced redundant memory access and control overhead. This design is suitable for low power FPGA based malware detection, where both latency and on chip resource usage are critical. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed sparse Linear Transformer can reduce hardware cost while preserving malware classification accuracy.

contribution.en: An event-sparse linear transformer and FPGA design reduce attention cost for malware detection.
contribution.zh: 事件稀疏线性Transformer与FPGA设计降低恶意软件检测的注意力开销。

why_care.en: It is an FPGA accelerator pipeline, not a compiler or IR contribution relevant to code generation.
why_care.zh: 这是FPGA加速器流水线，不是与代码生成相关的编译器或IR贡献。

candidates.title: ESL-former: Event Sparse Linear Transformer for FPGA-Accelerated Malware Detection

candidates.abstract: Long-output inference in large language models suffers from severe KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. While KV cache quantization alleviates this issue, low-bit quantization (e.g., 2-bit) severely degrades model accuracy. Recent mixed-precision key-cache quantization methods mitigate this degradation by allocating higher precision to important key channels, but estimate channel saliency using only key statistics. Through attention logit perturbation analysis at the RoPE channel-pair level, we show that quantization errors in channel pairs with large query--key pair-norm products contribute significantly to logit variation. Based on this insight, we propose PN-Mix, a mixed-precision key-cache quantization method for RoPE-based decoder-only LLMs, which allocates higher precision to salient channel pairs identified once during the prefill stage and reused throughout decoding. Across standard reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks, PN-Mix with 2.26-bit average precision achieves comparable or better average accuracy than prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32--2.39 bits. Furthermore, in our Pareto sweep, PN-Mix degrades gracefully down to 1.5 bits, whereas the compared baselines exhibit sharper performance drops below 2.25 bits.

contribution.en: PN-Mix uses RoPE pair-norm saliency to guide mixed-precision key-cache quantization.
contribution.zh: PN-Mix利用RoPE对范数显著性指导混合精度键缓存量化。

why_care.en: It is an LLM inference memory optimization with no compiler or architecture co-design angle.
why_care.zh: 这是LLM推理内存优化，没有编译器或架构协同设计角度。

candidates.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference

candidates.abstract: We introduce FormCraft, a framework for representing acquired operations as first-class capabilities that can be recursively composed, directly invoked, and selectively retained in a persistent library through domain-specific verification. The framework separates capability well-formedness and public callability from later admission to persistent storage while preserving formation provenance and operational identity. We formalize recursive compositional closure over a uniform capability space and show that formed composites can be reused through the same public interface without re-forming their historical derivation. Experiments across continuous, discrete, propositional, and sequence domains demonstrate instance-independent reuse, independent checking, persistent acquisition, and reduced reuse-time search work under first-class exposure.

contribution.en: FormCraft represents acquired operations as first-class, recursively composable capabilities with verification.
contribution.zh: FormCraft将习得操作表示为可递归组合且可验证的一等能力。

why_care.en: Its compositional capability reuse may inform program synthesis and IR-level modularity.
why_care.zh: 其组合式能力复用可能启发程序合成和IR级模块化。

candidates.title: Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities

candidates.abstract: Post-route power recovery changes cell choices under tightly coupled timing, electrical and physical constraints, and the value of each change depends on what it costs to repair its side effects. We propose an AI-driven framework in which a learned model drives both phases of the optimization: it ranks the powerrecovery edits to try and the repair actions that follow, while deterministic electronic design automation (EDA) analyses govern every acceptance. The framework records baseline constraint margins, identifies the damage a recovery transaction introduces in each analysis view, holds pre-existing violations at their baseline rather than working them inside the power step, and caps repair spending at a fraction of the measured saving. An ensemble of gradient-boosted models predicts power change, normalized damage reduction and constraint-regression risk from action and timing-context features available before each trial; calibrated, conservative estimates feed separate acquisition scores for recovery and repair, with a deterministic fallback when the model is uncertain. Recovery and repair remain speculative until physical implementation and fresh analysis establish baseline preservation and positive net saving. We specify the contract, the learned policy, the transactional flow and a pre-registered public evaluation protocol on open designs. Evidence from a companion study on public designs supports the contract; the learned policy is proposed, and no trained-model results or proprietary design measurements are reported.

contribution.en: An AI-driven, timing-aware EDA flow ranks power-recovery edits and repairs under deterministic checks.
contribution.zh: AI驱动且时序感知的EDA流程在确定性检查下排序功耗恢复编辑与修复。

why_care.en: It is an EDA backend optimization, not compiler optimization or retargetable code generation.
why_care.zh: 这是EDA后端优化，不是编译器优化或可重定向代码生成。

candidates.title: AI-Driven, Timing-Aware Power Optimization

candidates.abstract: Chemical chain-of-thought can contain hallucinated structural and property claims. We thereby introduce MolLean, a process-verifiable language that grounds chemical reasoning in an explicit molecular state. A layered Lean-based kernel checks state transitions and assertions over molecular readouts, from primitive graph edits to compound transformations. Meanwhile, a typed witness protocol separates native structural checks from externally supplied measurements. We further introduce MolLean-MCP, a stateful tool interface that exposes these transitions, checks, and readouts during generation: the model receives feedback to decide its next action, and rejected actions leave the state unchanged. MolLean supports one-pass trace execution, whole-trace refinement, and interactive reasoning through MolLean-MCP. We evaluate these three modes with direct chain-of-thought on 8,800 matched examples across 12 tasks spanning molecular generation, editing, optimization, and reactions. With Qwen3.6-27B, whole-trace refinement outperforms direct chain-of-thought on all 12 tasks. MolLean-MCP complements whole-trace refinement with stepwise verification feedback, reaching better performance in reaction tasks. Together, these results highlight an executable foundation for chemical reasoning, in which explicit chemical commitments can be checked and revised rather than remaining solely in free-form explanations.

contribution.en: Introduces a Lean-kernel-backed process-verifiable language for chemical reasoning with typed witness checks and a stateful MCP tool interface.
contribution.zh: 提出一种基于 Lean 内核的过程可验证化学推理语言，带类型化见证检查和有状态 MCP 工具接口。

why_care.en: Its verifiable state-transition and witness protocol may suggest ways to check compiler IR rewrites or synthesis traces.
why_care.zh: 其可验证状态转换与见证协议或可为检查编译器 IR 重写或合成轨迹提供思路。

candidates.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning

candidates.abstract: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods. Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison. To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods. Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, gains over GRPO remain limited in scope, with no method consistently outperforming it across settings. Second, strong final performance can mask unstable training. why_care.zh: 这是严谨的实证检验，但与编译器或体系结构研究的方法关联很小。

candidates.abstract: Model signing authenticates the full-precision weights W an LLM is released with, yet users run a quantized artifact Q whose producing transformation is not uniquely determined under current disclosure. We separate the non-environment inputs from the execution environment E and measure a quantity that, to our knowledge, has not been measured before: the Independent Verifiability Rate (IVR), the fraction of a popularity-sampled GGUF ecosystem that a third party can re-derive bit-for-bit. Across the 200 most-downloaded Hugging Face GGUF repositories (198 in scope), no artifact or model card records the build environment, so under a recorded-inputs protocol the IVR is 0/198. Yet the artifacts are not irreproducible. On four in-sample repositories that disclose their inputs, the card's information alone reproduces no Q4_K_M file, but two coordinates the card omits - the build's floating-point-contraction setting and, for hybrid models, the per-tensor quantization recipe - re-derive 7/8 target-quant files bit-for-bit on x86 (5/8 on arm64); the fp16 re-derives from the provider's checkpoint, but the calibration imatrix must be shipped and hash-bound, since recomputing it did not match. An older release additionally pins the instruction set and did not re-derive. Reproducing the divergence reported with llama.cpp PR #25353, we show that E is a necessary coordinate and that one compiler setting yields a unique output across the tested platforms at negligible quality cost (+0.06% perplexity). As a security characterization, benign floating-point non-determinism separates from uniformly placed nibble-flip tampering above a detection floor that grows with the environments a verifier must allow, but a targeted embedding edit evades the statistic, so the proposed protocol rests on exact re-derivation; adversarial-fp16 attacks lie outside it. We release the audit data and a re-runnable harness.

contribution.en: Measures an independent verifiability gap in quantized LLM supply chains and identifies compiler/build coordinates needed to re-derive GGUF artifacts bit-for-bit.
contribution.zh: 度量量化 LLM 供应链中的独立可验证性缺口，并指出逐比特复现 GGUF 产物所需的编译器/构建坐标。

why_care.en: Compiler settings and build environments are shown to determine binary reproducibility, a neighboring concern for compiler infrastructure.
why_care.zh: 编译器设置与构建环境决定二进制可复现性，这是编译器基础设施的一个邻近关切。

candidates.title: What You Sign Is Not What You Run: The Verifiability Gap in Quantized LLM Supply Chains

candidates.abstract: Computational compressive imaging, such as single-pixel imaging and lensless imaging, is a promising imaging technique, enabling the reconstruction of objects from under-sampled measurements through compressed sensing algorithms or deep learning methods. However, the demand for electronic computational resources grows rapidly when recovering high-resolution and multi-dimensional images and training neural networks with numerous parameters, which has become a bottleneck for the widespread adoption of this technique. Here, we propose a physics-driven reconstruction framework that formulates imaging inverse problems as Ising models and directly recovers target objects through the self-evolution of non-von Neumann Ising machines toward the ground state of the Hamiltonian. We employ a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver to demonstrate this proof-of-concept by reconstructing objects in both single-pixel imaging and a lensless diffuser camera at sampling rates ranging from 1% to 25%. By further incorporating a foreground-sparsity constraint and a smoothness constraint, the reconstruction quality of our method is comparable to or even better than that of mainstream algorithms. This approach has the potential to substantially reduce the electronic computational burden of inverse reconstruction, paving the way for real-time, low-power computational imaging.

contribution.en: Formulates compressive imaging inverse problems as Ising models and uses a simulated-annealing Ising solver for reconstruction with sparsity and smoothness constraints.
contribution.zh: 将计算压缩成像逆问题建模为 Ising 模型，并用模拟退火 Ising 求解器结合稀疏和平滑约束进行重建。

why_care.en: It applies non-von Neumann optimization hardware to imaging, which is only loosely related to compiler and PIM compilation interests.
why_care.zh: 它将非冯诺依曼优化硬件用于成像，仅与编译器和 PIM 编译兴趣松散相关。

candidates.title: Computational compressive imaging reconstruction with a simulated-annealing-based Ising solver

candidates.abstract: An edge server and nearby devices can train language models of different sizes together by mutual distillation. Federated unlearning (FU) and unlearning for large language models (LLMs) execute a removal request on one model. Under mutual distillation, however, the effect of the removed data has been copied into many students, and their uploads teach it back to the corrected teacher. We propose Holder-level Erasure via Replication-weighted Delta-closure (HERD), which decides which holders must be corrected. HERD records a knowledge lineage graph from the transfers that the server already performs and weights each edge by its transfer type. It computes how many times the residual at each holder will be copied and selects the cheapest set of holders whose correction bounds the cumulative residual after the request. A transfer guard and a rejoin rule cover the holders left uncorrected or offline. We prove that partial correction suffices only when the copy number of the lineage graph is below one, that averaging alone never reaches one, and that the correction set remains valid under link outages. On TOFU, HERD leaves 18% to 52% less cumulative residual than the strongest baseline at 6% to 12% of its correction cost.

contribution.en: Proposes HERD, a lineage-graph method that selects holders to correct for federated unlearning under mutual distillation while bounding residual knowledge.
contribution.zh: 提出 HERD，一种谱系图方法，在相互蒸馏下选择需纠正的持有者以限制残余知识。

why_care.en: Its graph-based correction selection is remote from compiler optimization and architecture research.
why_care.zh: 其基于图的纠正选择与编译器优化和体系结构研究相距甚远。

candidates.title: Tracing Knowledge Lineage for Federated Unlearning under Mutual Distillation

candidates.abstract: Spatial reception under directed molecule transport requires balancing useful molecule capture against intersymbol interference (ISI). To characterize this balance, we study a fully absorbing spherical receiver that counts absorption events only within a prescribed cap. Using the known joint first-hitting law under aligned drift, we derive exact cap impulse, cumulative, and eventual responses. We perform stable cumulative evaluation. We then assess the derived responses through particle simulations and time-step comparisons, and demonstrate that our conditional-timing analysis explains when opposite drifts of equal magnitude can favor the same wider aperture. We also show that for the studied geometry and a symbol duration of $0.15$ s, the aperture that maximizes the signal-to-interference difference (SID) increases from $29.13^\circ$ at zero drift to $61.86^\circ$ at a drift magnitude of $40$ $\mu$m/s. These results (i) connect joint arrival-time and location statistics to spatial reception design, (ii) characterize the tradeoff between useful molecule capture and ISI, (iii) support SID-based aperture selection for a given drift and symbol duration, and (iv) quantify the SID loss incurred by retaining the zero-drift optimal aperture for the same symbol duration.

contribution.en: Derives exact cap impulse, cumulative, and eventual responses for a spherical molecular communication receiver and uses them for aperture selection under drift.
contribution.zh: 推导漂移对齐下球形分子通信接收器的精确盖响应，并用于孔径选择。

why_care.en: It is a communication-theory result with no meaningful overlap with compiler or architecture work.
why_care.zh: 这是通信理论结果，与编译器或体系结构工作没有实质性重叠。

candidates.title: Exact Cap Response and Aperture Selection for Molecular Communication under Aligned Drift

candidates.abstract: Orthogonal transforms have emerged as an effective tool for low-bit quantization of large language models (LLMs), as they reshape activation distributions without changing the underlying model function. Existing approaches typically rely either on fixed data-agnostic transforms, such as Hadamard rotations, or on calibration-time optimization of learned rotations. We study rotation selection from first principles and show that maximizing covariance leads to spectral alignment and provides a principled criterion for constructing quantization-friendly orthogonal transforms. Based on this insight, we propose SpectrumQuant, a closed-form rotation method that estimates activation covariance from calibration data and uses it to construct a covariance-aware orthogonal transform for post-training quantization. Our formulation characterizes quantization-friendly rotations as compositions of alignment and mixing components, while recovering Hadamard matrices as a special case. Interestingly, a class of butterfly matrices belongs to this category. In the realm of LLM quantization, SpectrumQuant bridges the gap between data-agnostic structured rotations and learned rotations, providing an effective and efficient data-aware alternative for post-training quantization. Experiments on Llama and Mistral models show that SpectrumQuant is competitive with state-of-the-art rotation strategies while requiring less than one-third of the GPU memory and significantly less time than learned rotations approaches like SpinQuant and DartQuant.

contribution.en: Derives closed-form covariance-aware orthogonal rotations for LLM quantization, recovering Hadamard and butterfly transforms as special cases.
contribution.zh: 为 LLM 量化推导协方差感知的闭式正交旋转，并将 Hadamard 与蝴蝶变换作为特例。

why_care.en: It offers a principled transform for quantization, adjacent to tensor-compiler math but not central to compiler optimization.
why_care.zh: 它为量化提供有原则的变换，与张量编译器数学相邻但并非编译器优化核心。

candidates.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization

candidates.abstract: Much of Ethereum's most consequential code is immutable bytecode: old output of unverified compilers, and protocol logic run as contract code. We show that such bytecode can be verified as it is, without trusting what produced it, without simplifying the machine it runs on, and with no axioms beyond Lean's own. Blanc, a Lean 4 verification stack, reads fixed runtime bytes via kernel-checked certificates and states every theorem against Jaune, an executable semantics of the EVM and block processing that passes all 34,205 blockchain-test cases of Ethereum's fixture release v20.0.2 that involve only forks that have governed mainnet since May 2025. Eight artifacts, deployed from 2017 to 2026, come from seven compiler versions and an assembler. For the EIP-7002 contract, we prove that the end-of-block call to it, whose failure would invalidate the block, succeeds whatever its storage holds, and that each block's withdrawal requests are exactly the oldest pending submissions; mainnet met these theorems' starting premises when Prague began. For a Uniswap V2 pair, we prove that after any valid history whose hashed slots stay apart, from any checkpoint representing its Solidity model's state, the storage represents that model replayed over exactly the committed calls, a balanced liquidity ledger stays balanced, and, under a premise on token answers, geometric-mean reserves per share fall only through the protocol fee. Exact gas makes liveness provable: a tracked WETH9 holder without code can withdraw by a transaction whose gas has a closed form, matching all 3,748 comparable mainnet receipts of its shape in 30,000 blocks. On Curve pool bytes compiled with the lock bug exploited in 2023, Jaune executes such a reentrancy from deployment; for bytes from a fixed compiler, we prove the lock excludes it. AI agents wrote the proofs in fifteen days under one author's direction, atop an existing stack.

contribution.en: Verifies deployed EVM bytecode against executable EVM semantics with exact gas and no added axioms using a Lean 4 stack and kernel-checked certificates.
contribution.zh: 使用 Lean 4 验证栈和内核检查证书，依据可执行 EVM 语义精确验证已部署字节码及 gas，且不添加公理。

why_care.en: It demonstrates low-level bytecode verification with executable semantics, a neighboring technique for verified compilation and binary reasoning.
why_care.zh: 它展示基于可执行语义的低层字节码验证，是面向可信编译与二进制推理的邻近技术。

candidates.title: Verifying deployed bytecode against executable EVM semantics, with exact gas and no added axioms

recommendations.abstract: Sparse tensor compilers are commonly used high-performance tools that optimize tensor algebra programs over notoriously complex sparse data structures. Despite the ever-increasing size and scale of sparse datasets, there exists astonishingly little research on developing a parallel sparse tensor compiler. Existing approaches fail to parallelize or make assumptions about access patterns or output formats that limit generality. This paper presents Birdseed, the first tensor compiler to support all loop orderings over any standard sparse format in parallel. More specifically, Birdseed supports parallel sparse scatters and directly writes into list, bytemap, hash, and dense levels of fibertree sparse formats. Our approach exhibits asymptotic memory and time improvements over all previous work. We additionally demonstrate empirical speedups on challenging kernels to parallelize, such as histogram construction and SpMSpV.

contribution.en: Introduces Birdseed, the first tensor compiler supporting all loop orderings and parallel sparse outputs over standard sparse formats.
contribution.zh: 提出 Birdseed，首个支持所有循环顺序和任意标准稀疏格式并行稀疏输出的张量编译器。

why_care.en: Directly relates to tensor compilers, sparse code generation, and parallel compilation.
why_care.zh: 直接关联张量编译器、稀疏代码生成与并行编译。

recommendations.title: Parallel Sparse Outputs for Tensor Compilers

recommendations.abstract: Lane-based RISC-V vector processors exploit data parallelism well but pay a recurring cost for two common patterns: reductions, which require a separate tree pass, and deep dependent expression chains, which cannot be fused and are issued as serial vector instructions. We present TALU, a 5-stage RISC-V core whose execute stage is an NxN grid of registered ALU tiles instead of a single ALU. The grid is a reconfigurable, feed-forward spatial fabric: tiles route operands only from non-backward neighbours, and added diagonal forwarding lets a reduction collapse spatially. A minimal custom extension configures the per-tile operation, routing, and per-tile constants, and streams operands through the array. On a single fabric, TALU runs ordinary scalar code, single deep-path expressions, and multi-lane vector kernels. On the benchmark suite of the RISC-V2 vector processor, TALU is 1.8-5.5x faster than RISC-V2 and 4.5-15.5x faster than Vicuna at equal lane count, with a reduction cost (dot{\div}add) of 1.05x versus 1.96x and 1.26x for the vector cores. A retimed implementation places and routes at 1.03 GHz in 45 nm in 0.30 mm2, half the area of RISC-V2.

contribution.en: Introduces TALU, a reconfigurable N×N ALU-grid execute stage for RISC-V that accelerates reductions and deep dependent expressions.
contribution.zh: 提出 TALU，一种面向 RISC-V 的可重构 N×N ALU 网格执行级，加速规约和深依赖表达式。

why_care.en: Relevant to computer architecture, SIMD, and compiler-architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 与计算机体系结构、SIMD 和编译器-架构协同设计相关。

recommendations.title: TALU: A Reconfigurable Tiled-ALU Grid for RISC-V

recommendations.abstract: Analog in-memory computing performs the matrix-vector multiplications of neural networks directly inside the memory array, which saves time and energy. But each memory cell stores only a few levels and is noisy, so one cell cannot hold a weight precisely. The standard fix is to split each weight across several cells, like digits of a number. The base of this split decides the trade-off: a large base gives fine resolution but amplifies the noise, and a base near one averages the noise but wastes resolution. The best-known prior analysis considers only the noise, and so it always picks a base of one. We propose a principled method that also accounts for the limited number of levels per cell. It gives the optimal base in closed form, from a single measurement of the device noise. On a device-physics simulator, the optimal split is 3.3 dB more accurate than the common base-16 split, and it beats equal splitting in end-application accuracy.

contribution.en: Derives a closed-form optimal weight-splitting base for matrix-vector multiply on noisy analog in-memory accelerators, trading cell levels against device noise.
contribution.zh: 为噪声模拟存内计算中的矩阵向量乘提出闭式最优权重拆分基，同时权衡单元电平数和器件噪声。

why_care.en: Relevant to in-/near-memory compilation and mapping, offering a clean closed-form device-level optimization.
why_care.zh: 与存内计算/近存计算的编译与映射问题相关，且以简洁闭式解给出器件级优化。
